k: He lost his ring the day he went under. He always took the long way home — past the old chapel in the Drownmere.
src: 'He lost his ring the day he went under. He always took the long way home — past the old chapel in the Drownmere.'

k: I know it isn't really him. I know. But if he found it, maybe he'd stop walking.
src: 'I know it isn\'t really him. I know. But if he found it, maybe he\'d stop walking.'

k: We're going into the Drownmere anyway. We'll look.
src: 'We\'re going into the Drownmere anyway. We\'ll look.'

k: The Long Way Home
src: 'The Long Way Home'

k: Widow Pell's husband drowned with his wedding ring. Look for it near the old chapel in the Drownmere.
src: 'Widow Pell\'s husband drowned with his wedding ring. Look for it near the old chapel in the Drownmere.'

k: The punt bumps against a rotten jetty. Beyond it lies the Drownmere: black water, white fog, and a silence with something breathing in it.
src: 'The punt bumps against a rotten jetty. Beyond it lies the Drownmere: black water, white fog, and a silence with something breathing in it.'

k: Lovely. Really. Who wants to go first?
src: 'Lovely. Really. Who wants to go first?'

k: I do.
src: 'I do.'

k: Ilse — I'm the Warden, I should—
src: 'Ilse — I\'m the Warden, I should—'

k: You should stay behind me and be large.
src: 'You should stay behind me and be large.'

k: I can do that.
src: 'I can do that.'

k: Pale gold moss grows thick on the shrine stones, in the shape of the lamp that once stood here. It is warm, like a hand.
src: 'Pale gold moss grows thick on the shrine stones, in the shape of the lamp that once stood here. It is warm, like a hand.'

k: Lanternmoss. It drank the shrine-lamp's light for two hundred years. It still remembers.
src: 'Lanternmoss. It drank the shrine-lamp\'s light for two hundred years. It still remembers.'

k: It is humming. Like the forks. But _forwards_.
src: 'It is humming. Like the forks. But _forwards_.'

k: In the deepest hollow of the grotto, a single white lily grows out of the black mud, its petals closed tight.
src: 'In the deepest hollow of the grotto, a single white lily grows out of the black mud, its petals closed tight.'

k: A weepcap. It's never seen the sun — if light touches it, it wilts. Everybody, shade it.
src: 'A weepcap. It\'s never seen the sun — if light touches it, it wilts. Everybody, shade it.'

k: With what?
src: 'With what?'

k: With Bram.
src: 'With Bram.'

k: Happy to help!
src: 'Happy to help!'

k: Bram looms helpfully. Ilse lifts the lily out of the mud by its roots, as gently as lifting a sleeping child.
src: 'Bram looms helpfully. Ilse lifts the lily out of the mud by its roots, as gently as lifting a sleeping child.'

k: That's two. The third is whatever's making the rot. North, past the shrine island — the black pool.
src: 'That\'s two. The third is whatever\'s making the rot. North, past the shrine island — the black pool.'

k: Lanternmoss and a weepcap lily. Ilse knows exactly what she's doing. I'm mostly carrying things and trying not to fall in.
src: 'Lanternmoss and a weepcap lily. Ilse knows exactly what she\'s doing. I\'m mostly carrying things and trying not to fall in.'

k: One. Now the weepcap — the Root Grotto, east of the shrine island.
src: 'One. Now the weepcap — the Root Grotto, east of the shrine island.'

k: One. Now the lanternmoss — the Sunken Shrine, west of the shrine island.
src: 'One. Now the lanternmoss — the Sunken Shrine, west of the shrine island.'

k: A wall of black, rotted saplings chokes the path north. The wood is soft and wet and warm, and it is moving — very slightly, like something breathing.
src: 'A wall of black, rotted saplings chokes the path north. The wood is soft and wet and warm, and it is moving — very slightly, like something breathing.'

k: It's the rot. Grown solid.
src: 'It\'s the rot. Grown solid.'

k: It flinches from light. I can feel it flinch.
src: 'It flinches from light. I can feel it flinch.'

k: The lanternmoss would burn it, but it'll gutter out in a breath. I need the weepcap's sap to make it last. Lily first — the Root Grotto.
src: 'The lanternmoss would burn it, but it\'ll gutter out in a breath. I need the weepcap\'s sap to make it last. Lily first — the Root Grotto.'

k: We need something brighter than a torch. Something it remembers. Lanternmoss, from the Sunken Shrine.
src: 'We need something brighter than a torch. Something it remembers. Lanternmoss, from the Sunken Shrine.'

k: Ilse crushes a pinch of lanternmoss into a drop of weepcap sap and blows on it. It catches like a coal — a small, fierce, golden light.
src: 'Ilse crushes a pinch of lanternmoss into a drop of weepcap sap and blows on it. It catches like a coal — a small, fierce, golden light.'

k: The rot-wood shrivels from the light like a hand from a stove, and crumbles into wet black ash.
src: 'The rot-wood shrivels from the light like a hand from a stove, and crumbles into wet black ash.'

k: The sap makes the moss burn longer. Nana's book was right about everything.
src: 'The sap makes the moss burn longer. Nana\'s book was right about everything.'

k: Nana's book is always right.
src: 'Nana\'s book is always right.'

k: Don't tell her. She'll be unbearable.
src: 'Don\'t tell her. She\'ll be unbearable.'

k: On the drowned altar, half-buried in silt, something glints. A plain copper ring.
src: 'On the drowned altar, half-buried in silt, something glints. A plain copper ring.'

k: Inside the band, worn nearly smooth: _T. — always the long way home._
src: 'Inside the band, worn nearly smooth: _T. — always the long way home._'

k: Tobin Pell's ring. She'll want this back.
src: 'Tobin Pell\'s ring. She\'ll want this back.'

k: Someone's wedding ring. Someone in Mirefen might know whose.
src: 'Someone\'s wedding ring. Someone in Mirefen might know whose.'

k: The black pool is perfectly still. Bones ring its shore — fish, birds, something larger.
src: 'The black pool is perfectly still. Bones ring its shore — fish, birds, something larger.'

k: In the middle of the water, bubbles rise. Slowly. Like breathing.
src: 'In the middle of the water, bubbles rise. Slowly. Like breathing.'

k: I want it on record that I said "who wants to go first" and meant it rhetorically.
src: 'I want it on record that I said "who wants to go first" and meant it rhetorically.'

k: The pool heaves. Something rises out of it — a bloated, eyeless thing of black mud and gristle, ringed with mouths.
src: 'The pool heaves. Something rises out of it — a bloated, eyeless thing of black mud and gristle, ringed with mouths.'

k: That's it. That's the rot. That's what's in her lungs.
src: 'That\'s it. That\'s the rot. That\'s what\'s in her lungs.'

k: Then let's get it out.
src: 'Then let\'s get it out.'

k: When it is over, Ilse wades into the shallows with her knife and her jaw set, and comes back with something black and dense in a jar.
src: 'When it is over, Ilse wades into the shallows with her knife and her jaw set, and comes back with something black and dense in a jar.'

k: Rot-gall. The sickness, made solid.
src: 'Rot-gall. The sickness, made solid.'

k: You just — you just stuck your whole arm in that.
src: 'You just — you just stuck your whole arm in that.'

k: It was in Mother Osk's lungs. My arm can cope.
src: 'It was in Mother Osk\'s lungs. My arm can cope.'

k: We killed the thing in the black pool. Ilse cut its heart out and put it in a jar. I have never been so proud of anyone, or so glad she's on my side.
src: 'We killed the thing in the black pool. Ilse cut its heart out and put it in a jar. I have never been so proud of anyone, or so glad she\'s on my side.'

k: Ilse works for an hour without speaking. Moss, sap, gall — ground, steeped, strained. The Lantern fills with the smell of it.
src: 'Ilse works for an hour without speaking. Moss, sap, gall — ground, steeped, strained. The Lantern fills with the smell of it.'

k: Smells like a boot.
src: 'Smells like a boot.'

k: Like a boot that drowned and came back angry.
src: 'Like a boot that drowned and came back angry.'

k: Thank you both. Hold her head, Doctor.
src: 'Thank you both. Hold her head, Doctor.'

k: Ilse tips the draught between the old woman's lips, a spoonful at a time. Nobody breathes.
src: 'Ilse tips the draught between the old woman\'s lips, a spoonful at a time. Nobody breathes.'

k: Under Osk's skin, the black veins tremble — and begin, very slowly, to fade.
src: 'Under Osk\'s skin, the black veins tremble — and begin, very slowly, to fade.'

k: ...Who in the name of every frog in the fen fed me a _boot_?
src: '...Who in the name of every frog in the fen fed me a _boot_?'

k: Mother Osk!
src: 'Mother Osk!'

k: Hesk. You look terrible. Have you been making soup again? I can smell it from here.
src: 'Hesk. You look terrible. Have you been making soup again? I can smell it from here.'

k: Daft heron.
src: 'Daft heron.'

k: You. Girl. You did this.
src: 'You. Girl. You did this.'

k: With help.
src: 'With help.'

k: Your hands didn't shake.
src: 'Your hands didn\'t shake.'

k: They did. You just couldn't see.
src: 'They did. You just couldn\'t see.'

k: That's the whole trick of it, girl.
src: 'That\'s the whole trick of it, girl.'

k: And you're Ysolde's. I thought I dreamed you.
src: 'And you\'re Ysolde\'s. I thought I dreamed you.'

k: You called me by her name.
src: 'You called me by her name.'

k: I've known your mother since she was smaller than that scruffy one.
src: 'I\'ve known your mother since she was smaller than that scruffy one.'

k: Came to every Keepers' Conclave with her nose in a book. Just like you, I expect.
src: 'Came to every Keepers\' Conclave with her nose in a book. Just like you, I expect.'

k: Osk turns her head toward the brass cradle at the heart of the room. It is empty. She looks at it for a long time.
src: 'Osk turns her head toward the brass cradle at the heart of the room. It is empty. She looks at it for a long time.'

k: Hesk. Where's my stone.
src: 'Hesk. Where\'s my stone.'

k: They took it.
src: 'They took it.'

k: The Choir. The night your fever broke out. They had the Hierophant's seal. They said the Gloam was rising, that the stone was safer in the Cathedral, that they'd harmonize it and bring it home—
src: 'The Choir. The night your fever broke out. They had the Hierophant\'s seal. They said the Gloam was rising, that the stone was safer in the Cathedral, that they\'d harmonize it and bring it home—'

k: And you were saying "take it, take it, it's too heavy"—
src: 'And you were saying "take it, take it, it\'s too heavy"—'

k: I was talking about the _blanket_, you great soggy heron.
src: 'I was talking about the _blanket_, you great soggy heron.'

k: ...It's not your fault, boy. I'd told him no twice. To his face.
src: '...It\'s not your fault, boy. I\'d told him no twice. To his face.'

k: They didn't come for safekeeping. They came because I was too sick to say it a third time.
src: 'They didn\'t come for safekeeping. They came because I was too sick to say it a third time.'

k: Told _who_ no?
src: 'Told _who_ no?'

k: He wanted my stone. Said he needed all seven for something. A "harmony," he called it. He sent me one of those last spring.
src: 'He wanted my stone. Said he needed all seven for something. A "harmony," he called it. He sent me one of those last spring.'

k: Her eyes have gone to Wren's pack. Wren takes out the case of forks.
src: 'Her eyes have gone to Wren\'s pack. Wren takes out the case of forks.'

k: Put that away. I can hear it from here.
src: 'Put that away. I can hear it from here.'

k: I threw mine in the bog. Then the rot came up out of the bog. Make of that what you like.
src: 'I threw mine in the bog. Then the rot came up out of the bog. Make of that what you like.'

k: It sings to the others. All the forks, everywhere. They are waiting for something.
src: 'It sings to the others. All the forks, everywhere. They are waiting for something.'

k: ...Well. Aren't you a strange one. Come here, child. Let me see your face.
src: '...Well. Aren\'t you a strange one. Come here, child. Let me see your face.'
